## Curves, paths and shapes (since API\_MINOR 17)

three.js r185's curves, paths, shapes and ShapeUtils, statement by statement: the points they give are three.js's, natively and in browsers. Since API\_MINOR 20 the 3D curves too (`LineCurve3`, `QuadraticBezierCurve3`, `CubicBezierCurve3`, `CatmullRomCurve3`), each curve's `computeFrenetFrames`, `toJSON` and `fromJSON`, and paths of 3D curves.

### CurveJSON

*interface*

What a curve's `toJSON` gives (three.js's): its `type`, `arcLengthDivisions` and each kind's own fields (vectors as arrays).

```ts
export interface CurveJSON { … }
```

- `metadata?: { version: number; type: string; generator: string };`
- `type: string;`
- `arcLengthDivisions: number;`
- `[key: string]: any;`

### FrenetFrames

*interface*

Frenet frames along a curve: a tangent, normal and binormal at each of `segments + 1` points spaced by arc length.

```ts
export interface FrenetFrames { … }
```

- `tangents: Vector3[];`
- `normals: Vector3[];`
- `binormals: Vector3[];`

### Curve

*class*

A curve, 2D (`T` Vector2, the default) or 3D (Vector3, since API\_MINOR 20): `getPoint(t)` for t from 0 to 1 (each kind its own), and from it points spaced by arc length (`arcLengthDivisions` samples), lengths and tangents. A subclass of your own overrides `getPoint`.

```ts
export class Curve<T extends Vector2 | Vector3 = Vector2> { … }
```

- `type: string;`
- `arcLengthDivisions: number;`
- `needsUpdate: boolean;`
- `getPoint(t: number, optionalTarget?: T): T;`
- `getPointAt(u: number, optionalTarget?: T): T;`
- `getPoints(divisions?: number): T[];`
- `getSpacedPoints(divisions?: number): T[];`
- `getLength(): number;`
- `getLengths(divisions?: number): number[];`
- `updateArcLengths(): void;`
- `getUtoTmapping(u: number, distance?: number | null): number;`

- `getTangent(t: number, optionalTarget?: T): T;`

  The unit tangent at `t`, from points 0.0001 either side (a Vector2 or Vector3 as the curve's points are; a line's exactly).

- `getTangentAt(u: number, optionalTarget?: T): T;`

- `computeFrenetFrames(segments: number, closed?: boolean): FrenetFrames;`

  Tangents, normals and binormals at `segments + 1` points spaced by arc length (since API\_MINOR 20), as three.js computes them: the first normal across the first tangent's smallest axis, carried along by the turn between tangents; `closed` twists them evenly so the last meets the first. What TubeGeometry and ExtrudeGeometry's `extrudePath` follow.

- `clone(): this;`
- `copy(source: Curve<any>): this;`

- `toJSON(): CurveJSON;`

  Since API\_MINOR 20.

- `fromJSON(json: CurveJSON): this;`

  Since API\_MINOR 20: the curve set from `toJSON`'s data.

### ExtrudeGeometryOptions

*interface*

Since API\_MINOR 20, `extrudePath` extrudes along a 3D curve instead of +Z (`steps` layers at its `getSpacedPoints(steps)`, each shape point (x, y) placed along the frame's normal and binormal of `computeFrenetFrames(steps, closed)`, closed for a closed CatmullRomCurve3; no bevel and `depth` unused, as three.js), and a custom `UVGenerator` gives the UVs (before, either was a TypeError).

*interface*

```

### TubeGeometry

*class*

A tube of `radius` (default 1) round a 3D curve (three.js `TubeGeometry`; since API\_MINOR 20): `tubularSegments` (default 64) rings spaced along `path` by arc length, each of `radialSegments` (default 8) round the curve's Frenet frame there (`path.computeFrenetFrames(tubularSegments, closed)`, kept as `tangents`, `normals` and `binormals`); a `closed` tube's last ring is its first again. Indexed; UVs along (u) then round (v). Default: a quadratic Bézier from (-1, -1, 0) through (-1, 1, 0) to (1, 1, 0). Segment counts are whole numbers of 1 to 1,024 (else RangeError); built from a new curve or new segments, as three.js (a trail that grows makes a new one, or draws a range of one made long enough).

### Sky

*class*

Since API\_MINOR 40 (`SKY_MINOR`; absent before): three.js r185's addon `Sky` (examples/jsm/objects/Sky.js), exported here as the engine has no addons path (and from `starhermit:sky` too): Preetham's analytic daylight over a unit box seen from inside, with r185's clouds and sun disc, its program in WGSL. Its box's corners go to the far plane (three.js's `gl_Position.z = gl_Position.w`, a hair inside it), so `sky.scale.setScalar(450000)` shows it whatever the camera's far; it is not frustum-culled. Set it through `sky.material.uniforms` as in three.js: `turbidity` (2), `rayleigh` (1), `mieCoefficient` (0.005), `mieDirectionalG` (0.8), `sunPosition` (a Vector3), `up` ((0, 1, 0)), `cloudScale` (0.0002), `cloudSpeed` (0.0001), `cloudCoverage` (0.4), `cloudDensity` (0.4), `cloudElevation` (0.5), `showSunDisc` (1) and `time` (0). Its light is linear and tone mapped as three.js's (`tonemapping_fragment`). For a physically based sky with the time of day see `starhermit:sky`'s `SkyAtmosphere`.

```

## Materials

### MaterialParameters

*interface*

```ts
export interface MaterialParameters { … }
```

- `color?: ColorInput;`

  Base color (default white), linear; components above 1 (three.js HDR colors, up to 65504) light brighter than white, which tone mapping and bloom take.

- `map?: Texture | null;`

  Base color texture, multiplied by `color`.

- `opacity?: number;`

  0–1 (default 1). Below 1 needs `transparent` to blend.

- `transparent?: boolean;`

  Draws after opaque objects, sorted farthest first, blending as `blending` says (normal by default). Before API\_MINOR 20 blending other than normal draws there whatever this says; from it, as in three.js, this alone decides.

- `alphaTest?: number;`

  Above 0, pixels whose alpha is below it are discarded (masked).

- `blending?: Blending;`

- `blendEquation?: number;`

  With `CustomBlending` (since API\_MINOR 10): the color's equation (default `AddEquation`) and factors (default `SrcAlphaFactor` and `OneMinusSrcAlphaFactor`), and the alpha's (null, the default: the color's).

- `blendSrc?: number;`
- `blendDst?: number;`
- `blendEquationAlpha?: number | null;`
- `blendSrcAlpha?: number | null;`
- `blendDstAlpha?: number | null;`
- `side?: Side;`

- `shadowSide?: Side | null;`

  Since API\_MINOR 23: see `Material.shadowSide`.

- `depthWrite?: boolean;`

  Default from API\_MINOR 20: true, as three.js's for every material, transparent ones included. Before it: written unless blended, so a port declaring an older minor that relied on a transparent mesh's depth writes sets `depthWrite: true` (grid lines drawn before a glass top under them stay visible only where they wrote depth, as blended meshes draw farthest first).

- `depthTest?: boolean;`

  Whether the depth test applies (default true); without it the material draws whatever is nearer and writes no depth, as in three.js, whatever its `depthFunc`.

- `colorWrite?: boolean;`

  Since API\_MINOR 35: see `Material.colorWrite`.

- `depthFunc?: DepthModes;`

  The depth test's comparison (three.js `depthFunc`; a `DepthModes` constant such as `LessDepth`). Default: `LessEqualDepth` from API\_MINOR 20 (three.js's, so of two coplanar surfaces the later drawn shows), `LessDepth` before it (the earlier drawn shows). A value set is honoured at every minor: `LessDepth` keeps minor 19's coplanar result for a model whose faces were baked over each other. Shadow maps keep the nearer test. Another value is a TypeError at the frame's sync. Since engine 1.20.2 (any minor).

- `fog?: boolean;`

  Whether the scene's fog applies (default true).

- `vertexColors?: boolean;`

  Multiply by the geometry's `color` attribute.

- `polygonOffset?: boolean;`
- `polygonOffsetFactor?: number;`
- `polygonOffsetUnits?: number;`
- `visible?: boolean;`

- `premultipliedAlpha?: boolean;`

  With `transparent` and normal blending: the output's color times its alpha over earlier output times one minus the alpha (three.js `premultipliedAlpha`; since API\_MINOR 7). A built-in material's color is premultiplied for it; a ShaderMaterial's fragment gives its color premultiplied, so alpha 0 adds light (glows and smoke in one material).

- `toneMapped?: boolean;`

  Whether the output is tone mapped (default true; post effects tone map everything). Since API\_MINOR 6.

- `hooks?: MaterialHooks | null;`

  Hooks into the material's shading (since API\_MINOR 6).

### Material

*class*

Common to all materials; changes apply from the next frame.

```ts
export abstract class Material { … }
```

- `#private;`

- `readonly id: number;`

  three.js's (since API\_MINOR 20): a number of its own, in the order materials are made; from API\_MINOR 20 it orders the opaque list after render order.

- `name: string;`
- `userData: Record<string, unknown>;`
- `color: Color;`
- `map: Texture | null;`
- `opacity: number;`
- `transparent: boolean;`
- `alphaTest: number;`
- `blending: Blending;`

- `blendEquation: number;`

  Since API\_MINOR 10: see `MaterialParameters.blendEquation`.

- `blendSrc: number;`
- `blendDst: number;`
- `blendEquationAlpha: number | null;`
- `blendSrcAlpha: number | null;`
- `blendDstAlpha: number | null;`
- `side: Side;`

- `shadowSide: Side | null;`

  The faces the shadow maps draw (three.js; since API\_MINOR 23): null (the default) draws the side opposite `side` (back faces of a front-sided material, front faces of a back-sided one, both of a double-sided one), so a surface facing the light is not in its own map and does not shadow itself. Before API\_MINOR 23 the maps draw the faces `side` draws, and this is ignored.

- `depthWrite: boolean;`
- `depthTest: boolean;`

- `colorWrite: boolean;`

  Since API\_MINOR 35 (`COLOR_WRITE_MINOR`; absent before): three.js r185's `colorWrite` (default true). False draws no color: the material's draws still test and write depth as `depthTest` and `depthWrite` say (a depth-only occluder or mask, a depth prime); shadow maps and `renderer.sceneDepth` take it as before. Every backend masks the color target's writes in the draw's pipeline.

- `depthFunc: DepthModes;`

  Since engine 1.20.2 (any minor): see `MaterialParameters.depthFunc`. Reads the default the game's minor takes until one is set.

- `fog: boolean;`
- `vertexColors: boolean;`
- `polygonOffset: boolean;`
- `polygonOffsetFactor: number;`
- `polygonOffsetUnits: number;`
- `visible: boolean;`

- `envMap: Texture | null;`

  An environment this material reflects instead of `scene.environment` (standard, physical, Lambert and, since API\_MINOR 29, Phong materials; see `PMREMGenerator`).

- `toneMapped: boolean;`

  Since API\_MINOR 6: whether the output is tone mapped (three.js `toneMapped`, default true; without post effects only).

- `premultipliedAlpha: boolean;`

  Since API\_MINOR 7: see `MaterialParameters.premultipliedAlpha`.

- `hooks: MaterialHooks | null;`

  Since API\_MINOR 6: the game's WGSL hooked into this material's shading (standard, physical, Lambert and basic materials, and Phong, toon and matcap ones since API\_MINOR 29; see `MaterialHooks`), or null. Assign a new object, or change its sources or uniforms' types, and the material's program follows from the next frame; uniform values are read every frame.

- `readonly shaderError: string | null;`

  Since API\_MINOR 6: why the material's program was refused, as `part:line:column: message` (the part being `vertex`, `surface`, `vertexShader`, `fragmentShader`, `uniforms` or `engine`), or null. A refused program leaves the material drawing without it (a `ShaderMaterial` draws nothing) and is logged once. The engine checks the code by the rules browsers' WebGPU enforces, but a browser's WebGPU compiles the program again as the game draws on and may still refuse it some frames later: the game's log then says so once (with WebGPU's message at the part, line and column), and `shaderError` reports it from then on.

- `compile(): void;`

  Since API\_MINOR 6: compiles the material's program now (otherwise it compiles when first drawn), throwing a SyntaxError with `shaderError`'s message if it is refused.

- `clone(): this;`

  A material of the same class with this one's settings: colors and vectors copied, textures shared (three.js); since API\_MINOR 18 its userData copied by JSON and a ShaderMaterial's uniforms cloned.

- `copy(source: Material): this;`

  `source`'s settings, as `clone` takes them (since API\_MINOR 18).

- `dispose(): void;`

## Custom materials (since API\_MINOR 6)

A game's WGSL (the WebGPU shading language; the subset starhermit-shader compiles: no switch, while, pointers or atomics) joined with the engine's mesh stages and compiled for every backend (SPIR-V, HLSL, GLSL ES 3.00, WGSL), so the same code draws on Vulkan, Direct3D 12, OpenGL ES, WebGPU and WebGL2. It is sandboxed: a part declares structs, constants and functions only (no variables, bindings, entry points or attributes, no names the engine declares, nothing starting with `_`), reads no engine globals but `uniforms` and its textures, and loops only with `for (var i = A; i < B; i++)` over constant bounds and step (any of &lt;, &lt;=, &gt;, &gt;=, ++, --, += k, -= k; at most 65,536 iterations, nested loops together); WGSL has no recursion. Derivatives (dpdx, dpdy, fwidth), textureSample and textureSampleBias stay in uniform control flow (outside branches and loops on per-pixel values; branching on `uniforms` and constants is fine), as WebGPU requires; vertex code samples with textureSampleLevel or textureSampleGrad and cannot discard. textureSampleBias, textureSampleGrad (explicit gradients, so anywhere) and textureDimensions (a texture's size, or a mip level's) work on every backend since API\_MINOR 8. Each part is at most 64 KiB. Errors name the part and its own line and column.

What the engine declares for a game's code:

```text
struct Vertex { position: vec3f, normal: vec3f, uv: vec2f,
  color: vec4f, custom: vec4f, instance: vec4f, clip: vec4f,
  v0: vec4f, v1: vec4f, v2: vec4f, v3: vec4f,
  instance_color: vec4f, vertex_color: vec4f,
  instance1: vec4f, instance2: vec4f, instance3: vec4f }
  position and normal in object space; color the instance color times
  the vertex color (when the material has vertexColors; white
  otherwise), each also given alone (instance_color, which includes
  the InstancedMesh's color, 0..65504, and vertex_color: a game may
  carry data in them and set color itself); custom the
  geometry's `custom` attribute (zeros without one); instance the
  InstancedMesh's `instanceCustom` slot 0 and instance1..3 its slots
  1 to 3 (zeros otherwise); clip zero, or
  set by the hook (w not 0) to place the vertex in clip space itself
  (depth -1..1 as view_projection() gives; the shadow pass ignores
  it); v0..v3 four varyings for the fragment stage.
struct Surface { base_color: vec4f, emissive: vec3f, metalness: f32,
  roughness: f32, normal: vec3f, occlusion: f32, world: vec3f,
  uv: vec2f, color: vec4f, v0..v3: vec4f, front: bool }
  base_color linear after the map, color, opacity and vertex colors;
  emissive linear after its intensity and map; normal in world space
  after the normal map; occlusion 0..1 (1 none). The rest describe the
  fragment (read-only).
struct Fragment { world: vec3f, normal: vec3f, uv: vec2f, color: vec4f,
  v0..v3: vec4f, front: bool, coord: vec4f }
  coord the fragment's window position (WGSL @builtin(position);
  rows from the top on every backend since API_MINOR 8, where OpenGL
  ES and WebGL2 windows had counted them from the bottom).
struct Light { sun: vec3f, shadow: f32, direct: vec3f,
  indirect: vec3f, emissive: vec3f, sun_direction: vec3f,
  sun_color: vec3f, ambient: vec3f, world: vec3f, normal: vec3f,
  uv: vec2f, base_color: vec4f, v0..v3: vec4f }   (since API_MINOR 9)
  sun the primary light's reflected light without its shadow and
  shadow that shadow (1 lit, 0 shadowed); direct the other lights'
  (their shadows applied); indirect ambient, hemisphere and
  environment light (ambient occlusion applied); emissive the
  surface's. The rest read-only: sun_direction toward the primary
  light, its color, the ambient color, and the fragment (normal the
  shading normal facing the viewer, the surface's base color and
  varyings).
struct Fog { color: vec3f, amount: f32, world: vec3f, depth: f32,
  coord: vec4f, camera: vec3f }               (since API_MINOR 9)
  color linear and amount 0 (none) to 1 (full): the scene's fog
  (black and 0 without one); fogged in display color as the scene's
  fog is (or in linear light before the post effects' tone mapping).
  Read-only: the fragment's world position, view depth and window
  position (rows from the top, for screen_uv, renderer.sceneDepth
  and renderer.sceneColor)
  and the camera's position.
fn model_matrix() -> mat4x4f       object to world, instance included
fn vertex_index() -> u32           (both vertex stage only)
fn view_projection() -> mat4x4f    world to clip (depth -1..1)
fn camera_position() -> vec3f
fn viewport_size() -> vec2f        in pixels
fn srgb_to_linear(c: vec3f) -> vec3f, fn linear_to_srgb(c: vec3f) -> vec3f
fn view_depth(world: vec3f) -> f32  distance along the camera's
                                   forward axis (since API_MINOR 8)
fn screen_uv(coord: vec4f) -> vec2f a window position as texture
                                   coordinates, 0..1 from the top
                                   left (since API_MINOR 8)
fn pass_kind() -> u32              the pass the hook runs in
                                   (since API_MINOR 26): PASS_MAIN
                                   (the lit pass), PASS_SHADOW (a
                                   shadow map's) or PASS_PREPASS
                                   (the depth or normal prepass)
fn is_shadow_pass() -> bool        pass_kind() == PASS_SHADOW: e.g.
                                   a hook that dithers its surface
                                   in view keeps its shadow solid
                                   (since API_MINOR 26; games below
                                   it may declare these names)
fn linear_fog() -> bool            whether this pass fogs in linear
                                   light (drawn through post
                                   buffers, tone mapped after) rather
                                   than in display color (an engine
                                   extension, since API_MINOR 40)
fn tone_mapped(c: vec3f) -> vec3f  a linear color tone mapped as
                                   this fragment's is where the pass
                                   draws straight (the renderer's
                                   tone mapping and exposure; c for
                                   a material not tone mapped; since
                                   API_MINOR 40)
```

Textures are RGBA8 as uploaded (a Uint8Array DataTexture's bytes as they are, read as 0..1; since API\_MINOR 25 a float or half-float DataTexture's values as they are, below 0 and above 1, in half-float precision): for exact texels (data, animation frames), use NearestFilter and sample texel centers, (i + 0.5) / size, with textureSampleLevel, which vertex code also uses; or, since API\_MINOR 10, read one exactly, whatever the filter, with

```text
textureLoad(NAME, vec2i(x, y), 0) -> vec4f   (vec2u too)
```

level 0 only (the literal 0); x and y are clamped into the texture on every runtime (WebGPU included), so outside it they read the texel at its edge. Texture coordinates are WGSL's: (0, 0) is the image's first row as uploaded (an image file's top, a DataTexture's first row of data) and v grows down it. The geometry's uv arrives turned to that convention (Vertex.uv, Surface.uv and Fragment.uv are three.js's uv with v replaced by 1 - v), so sampling with them shows a texture as a built-in map does; coordinates a hook computes itself (an atlas cell, a texel of data) count rows from the first. Ported three.js GLSL that computes v upward from the bottom (or reads vUv.y) uses 1 - v. Porting three.js GLSL, two differences to watch:

```text
- vUv.y is 1.0 - uv.y here (uv.x is the same): a gradient, stripe or
  mask over vUv.y reads `let v = 1.0 - f.uv.y;` (Vertex, Surface and
  Fragment alike); texture sampling takes uv as it is.
- smoothstep(e0, e1, x) with e0 > e1 is undefined in WGSL (WebGPU
  may return anything; three's GLSL ports rely on the reversed ramp,
  which GLSL also leaves undefined but GPUs happen to compute):
  write `1.0 - smoothstep(e1, e0, x)` instead of
  `smoothstep(e0, e1, x)` when e0 > e1.
var<uniform> uniforms: Uniforms    the material's uniforms by name
NAME: texture_2d<f32>, NAME_sampler: sampler   each texture uniform
(a DataArrayTexture's NAME is a texture_2d_array<f32>; since
API_MINOR 25, see DataArrayTexture; a Data3DTexture's or a
WebGL3DRenderTarget's texture a texture_3d<f32>; since API_MINOR 35,
see Data3DTexture)
const NAME                          each define
```

The hooks, each optional:

```text
fn vertex(v: Vertex) -> Vertex     every pass: the shadows and the
                                   occlusion prepass see the same shape
fn surface(s: Surface) -> Surface  before light, shadows and fog (and
                                   the alpha test); may discard, in the
                                   shadow pass too
                                   On an unlit MeshBasicMaterial the
                                   color is base_color plus emissive
                                   (a glow), its alpha base_color's
                                   (vertex alpha included), blended
                                   as the material says (additive
                                   for glows).
fn light(l: Light) -> Light       (since API_MINOR 9) lit materials:
                                   the light the surface reflects, by
                                   kind, before it is added up as
                                   sun × shadow + direct + indirect +
                                   emissive (under a clearcoat): tinted
                                   shadows (add a tint where shadow < 1),
                                   cloud shadows (shadow times a cloud
                                   texture sampled at world.xz)
fn fog(f: Fog) -> Fog             (since API_MINOR 9; both kinds) the
                                   fog on the fragment: height fog or
                                   mist from world.y and depth, with or
                                   without the scene's fog; not run for
                                   materials with `fog` false
```

A ShaderMaterial's instead of surface (required):

```text
fn fragment(f: Fragment) -> vec4f  linear color and alpha, then fog
                                   (with `fog`) and tone mapping (with
                                   `toneMapped`) as other materials
```

Programs with identical sources, defines and uniform types share one; a game holds at most 256 (RangeError). Points and sprites take no hooks.

### ShaderUniform

*interface*

A uniform: `value` is read every frame. Its type follows the value: a number is `f32`; Vector2, Vector3 (or Color, linear) and Vector4 (or Quaternion) are `vec2f`, `vec3f`, `vec4f`; a Matrix4 `mat4x4f`; an array of Vector4 or Matrix4, or a Float32Array of 4n numbers, an `array<vec4f, n>` or `array<mat4x4f, n>`; a Texture (or null, the white texture) a texture and sampler (at most 5 a material since API\_MINOR 9, 4 before: with the material's own maps and the shadow maps that is the 16 a WebGL2 fragment stage is sure to sample; since API\_MINOR 34 a `ShaderMaterial`, which replaces the material's maps, up to 12, the sixth on taking the maps' places, all readable in both stages; hooks keep 5; API\_MINOR 35 keeps 12: with the four shadow maps a fragment stage then samples the 16 WebGPU, WebGL2, OpenGL ES and Vulkan are sure of, so pack more as the layers of an array texture or the channels of one). A `DataArrayTexture` (since API\_MINOR 25) or a `WebGLArrayRenderTarget`'s texture (since 34) is a `texture_2d_array<f32>`; a `Data3DTexture` or a `WebGL3DRenderTarget`'s texture (since 35) a `texture_3d<f32>`, one of the textures. Each member takes whole vec4 slots, 16,384 bytes in all since API\_MINOR 10 (4,096 before; 1,024 vec4s, 256 matrices: WebGL2's least uniform block): a larger block is refused (`compile()` throws a SyntaxError, the material draws without its program).

```ts
export interface ShaderUniform { … }
```

- `value: number | Vector2 | Vector3 | Vector4 | Color | Quaternion | Matrix4 | Texture | null | readonly Vector4[] | readonly Matrix4[] | Float32Array;`

### MaterialHooks

*interface*

The game's WGSL hooked into a built-in material (three.js `onBeforeCompile`, cleanly).

```ts
export interface MaterialHooks { … }
```

- `uniforms?: Record<string, ShaderUniform>;`

- `defines?: Record<string, number | boolean>;`

  WGSL constants (three.js `defines`): whole numbers become abstract integers, other numbers f32, booleans bool. At most 64.

- `vertex?: string;`

  Declares `fn vertex(v: Vertex) -> Vertex`.

- `surface?: string;`

  Declares `fn surface(s: Surface) -> Surface`.

- `light?: string;`

  Declares `fn light(l: Light) -> Light` (since API\_MINOR 9; lit materials).

- `fog?: string;`

  Declares `fn fog(f: Fog) -> Fog` (since API\_MINOR 9).

### ShaderMaterialParameters

*interface*

```ts
export interface ShaderMaterialParameters extends MaterialParameters { … }
```

- `uniforms?: Record<string, ShaderUniform>;`
- `defines?: Record<string, number | boolean>;`

- `vertexShader?: string;`

  WGSL declaring `fn vertex(v: Vertex) -> Vertex` (optional).

- `fragmentShader?: string;`

  WGSL declaring `fn fragment(f: Fragment) -> vec4f`. Since API\_MINOR 38 (`MRT_MINOR`) it may instead return a struct the same code declares, each member a `vec4f` with one `@location(n)` (`n` 0 to 7, each once, 0 among them; the only attributes a game's WGSL carries): a `WebGLRenderTarget` with `count` gets texture `n` from member `n` (see there); elsewhere location 0 alone is drawn.

- `fogShader?: string;`

  WGSL declaring `fn fog(f: Fog) -> Fog` (since API\_MINOR 9; with `fog: true`).

- `straightToneMapping?: boolean;`

  Since API\_MINOR 36 (`STRAIGHT_TONE_MINOR`): see `ShaderMaterial.straightToneMapping`.

### ShaderMaterial

*class*

The game's own surface and light (three.js `ShaderMaterial`, in WGSL; since API\_MINOR 6): `fragmentShader` gives each fragment's linear color. Blending, sides, depth, render order, shadows (cast without discard) and `alphaTest` work as for other materials; `fog` defaults to false. A refused program draws nothing.

```ts
export class ShaderMaterial extends Material { … }
```

- `constructor(parameters?: ShaderMaterialParameters);`
- `uniforms: Record<string, ShaderUniform>;`
- `defines: Record<string, number | boolean>;`
- `vertexShader: string;`
- `fragmentShader: string;`

- `fogShader: string;`

  Since API\_MINOR 9 (see `ShaderMaterialParameters`).

- `straightToneMapping: boolean;`

  Since API\_MINOR 36 (`STRAIGHT_TONE_MINOR`; older games' materials have no such property), default false. With `premultipliedAlpha` the fragment still gives its color premultiplied, and the renderer divides it by its alpha, tone maps, encodes and fogs that straight color, then multiplies it by the alpha again: three.js's order for a shader ending in `tonemapping_fragment`, `colorspace_fragment`, `fog_fragment` and `premultiplied_alpha_fragment`, so a thin edge (small alpha) is not brighter than the body behind it. Light given at alpha 0 is output as given (it has no straight color). Without it the premultiplied color is tone mapped and encoded as given (a three.js shader writing premultiplied color before those chunks), as before. Post effects tone map the composite either way.

  Scales the environment's light (default 1): its `envMap`'s, or the scene's (`scene.environment`) times `scene.environmentIntensity`. Until host API 1.18, and again from API\_MINOR 20, the scene's environment takes only `environmentIntensity`, as three.js r163 and later's WebGLRenderer does (it overrides the material's with it); three.js r162 and earlier, and its WebGPURenderer, take the material's, as API\_MINOR 18 and 19 do.

- `bumpMap: Texture | null;`

  Since API\_MINOR 18: a height map whose red channel's screen-space slope tilts the normal (three.js's derivative bump mapping, `perturbNormalArb`), scaled by `bumpScale` (default 1, within ±16); three.js reads it only without a `normalMap`, and so does the runtime. It takes the normal map's UVs and its own transform.

- `bumpScale: number;`

- `flatShading: boolean;`

  Since API\_MINOR 18: faceted shading, each fragment its triangle's normal from the screen-space derivatives of its position (facing the viewer, as three.js's shader makes it), the geometry's normals unused and unchanged.

- `wireframe: boolean;`

  Since API\_MINOR 18: draws each triangle's three edges as lines one pixel wide (three.js's renderer's wireframe index: an edge two triangles share is drawn twice), shaded per pixel as the material shades its surface (lit materials light them with the geometry's normals). A wireframe casts no shadow (three.js's casts its lines'), is left out of ambient occlusion, runs no custom hooks, and rays hit its triangles as three.js's do. Meshes, material arrays' groups and instanced meshes draw it; other meshes (a glTF's, skinned ones) draw filled.

- `wireframeLinewidth: number;`

  Kept, and always 1 (WebGL draws one-pixel lines).

- `wireframeLinecap: string;`
- `wireframeLinejoin: string;`

## The scene graph

### Object3D

*class*

```ts
export class Object3D { … }
```

- `constructor();`

- `uuid: string;`

  three.js's (since API\_MINOR 25; made when first read): the animation mixer's key, and a track may name a node by it.

- `name: string;`
- `readonly position: Vector3;`

- `readonly rotation: Euler;`

  Linked with `quaternion` (see `Euler`); the runtime reads the quaternion once a frame after `onRender`.

- `readonly quaternion: Quaternion;`
- `readonly scale: Vector3;`

- `readonly matrix: Matrix4;`

  Local and world transforms, kept up to date as three.js's `updateMatrixWorld` would (reading them is always current). While `matrixAutoUpdate` is false, `matrix` is the object's own (since API\_MINOR 26, as three.js): set it (`matrix.fromArray`, `copy`) to place the object and what is under it; `updateMatrix()` composes it from position, quaternion and scale. It draws decomposed (a shear is lost). Older minors always compose it.

- `readonly matrixWorld: Matrix4;`

  Before API\_MINOR 34 each read composes the local matrix and multiplies it into the parent's world matrix, which is read the same way: O(depth) compositions and multiplications a read. Since API\_MINOR 34 an object keeps its world matrix between reads and makes it again only when its position, quaternion or scale (or, while `matrixAutoUpdate` is false, its own `matrix`'s elements), its parent, or its parent's world matrix changed, compared bit for bit: a read walks the chain comparing those numbers (O(depth) compares), then composes and multiplies where something changed, with the same float operations, so every read gives the numbers an uncached read gives (likewise `getWorldPosition`, `getWorldQuaternion`, `getWorldScale`, `getWorldDirection`, `localToWorld`, `worldToLocal` and `lookAt`). The matrices handed out stay as an uncached read leaves them: `matrixWorld` returns the same Matrix4 each read, written with the current numbers, and once handed out it is written again at each read through the object or under it, as before. No call is needed after changing a transform, as before: `updateMatrixWorld` and `updateWorldMatrix` still do nothing.

- `visible: boolean;`

- `renderOrder: number;`

  Lower draws first among opaque objects, and among blended ones before they sort farthest first (three.js `renderOrder`). From API\_MINOR 20 a `Group`'s orders everything under it first (three.js's `groupOrder`, up to the next Group).

- `castShadow: boolean;`

  Since API\_MINOR 18 a mesh with a transparent (blended) material casts too, its depth whole as an opaque one's, whatever its opacity (three.js); games declaring older minors' cast none.

- `receiveShadow: boolean;`

- `frustumCulled: boolean;`

  Whether a mesh out of view (by its geometry's bounds, or for an InstancedMesh each run of instances by theirs) is left out (default true; three.js; since API\_MINOR 7). False draws it wherever it is, as a custom material's vertex hook may place it (positions all zero, set from `vertex_index()`, need no bounds): its bounds then decide nothing, in the view or in shadow maps; an InstancedMesh then keeps its instances exactly as given, as three.js draws them: in order, singular matrices kept (data a hook reads through `model_matrix()`, composed with the mesh's own transform: keep the mesh at the origin), mirrored ones drawn with the mesh's winding. Culled (the default), instances are arranged by place, a singular one's columns zeroed (it draws nothing) and mirrored ones drawn with their faces turned the right way.

- `noAO: boolean;`

  Leaves the object and its descendants out of `renderer.ao` (default false; since API\_MINOR 4): they cast no ambient occlusion, and where they are drawn the occlusion of what lies behind them applies (sky domes, light cones, nets). Sprites and points never take part.

- `readonly parent: Object3D | null;`
- `readonly children: readonly Object3D[];`

- `userData: Record<string, unknown>;`

  The game's own data (never read by the runtime).

- `add(...objects: Object3D[]): this;`

  Moves objects here from wherever they were. A cycle throws a TypeError; past the scene's bounds, a RangeError.

- `remove(...objects: Object3D[]): this;`
- `removeFromParent(): this;`
- `clear(): this;`

- `lookAt(target: Vector3): void;`

  Turns -Z (cameras, lights) or +Z (other objects) toward a world point.

- `lookAt(x: number, y: number, z: number): void;`
- `getWorldPosition(target: Vector3): Vector3;`
- `getWorldQuaternion(target: Quaternion): Quaternion;`
- `getWorldDirection(target: Vector3): Vector3;`
- `rotateX(angle: number): this;`
- `rotateY(angle: number): this;`
- `rotateZ(angle: number): this;`
- `rotateOnAxis(axis: Vector3, angle: number): this;`
- `translateX(distance: number): this;`
- `translateY(distance: number): this;`
- `translateZ(distance: number): this;`

- `updateMatrixWorld(force?: boolean): void;`

  Kept for ports; matrices are always current.

- `localToWorld(vector: Vector3): Vector3;`
- `worldToLocal(vector: Vector3): Vector3;`
- `traverse(callback: (object: Object3D) => void): void;`
- `getObjectByName(name: string): Object3D | undefined;`

Since API\_MINOR 18.

- `readonly layers: Layers;`

  The layers a Raycaster tests it on (layer 0 by default). Since API\_MINOR 35 (`LAYERS_MINOR`) also the layers the renderer tests, as three.js r185's: a pass (`renderer.render` into a target, and the window's frame) draws an object only when `object.layers.test( camera.layers)`, what is under it tested in turn; a light outside the camera's layers lights nothing and casts no shadow, and an object outside them casts none either (three.js's shadow maps test the camera's layers). A camera's own `layers` say what it sees. Older games' renderers draw every visible object whatever its layers.

- `animations: unknown[];`

  three.js's (kept, not played).

- `clone(recursive?: boolean): this;`

  An object of the same class with this one's settings and, unless `recursive` is false, clones of its children, as three.js's: meshes, points, lines and sprites share their geometry and material (an array copied), an InstancedMesh copies its instances' matrices, colors and custom values, cameras and lights copy their settings (a light's target is cloned), userData is copied by JSON. A glTF model's `gltf.scene.clone()` is a copy to add as often as wanted, sharing the model's geometry and materials. A class of the game's own is made with no constructor arguments, as in three.js. The scene cannot be cloned (TypeError).

- `copy(source: Object3D, recursive?: boolean): this;`

  `source`'s settings (name, up, position, rotation, quaternion, scale, matrixAutoUpdate, layers, visible, castShadow, receiveShadow, noAO, frustumCulled, renderOrder, animations, userData by JSON) and, unless `recursive` is false, clones of its children added here.

- `readonly up: Vector3;`
- `matrixAutoUpdate: boolean;`
- `getObjectById(id: number): Object3D | undefined;`
- `getObjectByProperty(name: string, value: unknown): Object3D | undefined;`
- `getObjectsByProperty(name: string, value: unknown, result?: Object3D[]): Object3D[];`
- `traverseVisible(callback: (object: Object3D) => void): void;`
- `traverseAncestors(callback: (object: Object3D) => void): void;`
- `getWorldScale(target: Vector3): Vector3;`
- `rotateOnWorldAxis(axis: Vector3, angle: number): this;`
- `translateOnAxis(axis: Vector3, distance: number): this;`
- `attach(object: Object3D): this;`

- `applyMatrix4(matrix: Matrix4): this;`

  Its transform becomes `matrix` times it.

- `applyQuaternion(q: Quaternion): this;`

### LOD

*class*

three.js r185's `LOD` (since API\_MINOR 26): of its levels (children added by `addLevel`), the one for the camera's distance shows, the rest are made invisible. The distance is from the camera's world position to the LOD's, divided by the camera's `zoom`; a level already showing keeps showing until `hysteresis` (a fraction of its distance) nearer. With `autoUpdate` the renderer updates it every frame for the camera it draws (and in `renderer.render` for that call's camera), as three.js's `WebGLRenderer` does for LODs under visible parents, before shadow maps draw: shadows cast from the level the camera sees. Before API\_MINOR 35 the engine draws whatever the objects' layers, so the update does not test them; from 35 (`LAYERS_MINOR`), as three.js, only a LOD whose layers meet the camera's is updated. Before API\_MINOR 26 the constructor is a TypeError.

```ts
export class LOD extends Object3D { … }
```

- `constructor();`
- `readonly isLOD: true;`
- `readonly type: "LOD";`

- `readonly levels: LODLevel[];`

  Its levels, nearest first.

- `autoUpdate: boolean;`

  Whether the renderer updates it each frame (default true).

- `addLevel(object: Object3D, distance?: number, hysteresis?: number): this;`

  Adds `object` (as a child) shown from `distance` (its absolute value) on.

- `removeLevel(distance: number): boolean;`

  Removes the level at exactly `distance` (and its object).

- `getCurrentLevel(): number;`

  The index of the level the last update chose.

- `getObjectForDistance(distance: number): Object3D | null;`

- `update(camera: Camera): void;`

  Shows the level for `camera`'s distance (three.js's).

### Mesh

*class*

```ts
export class Mesh<TMaterial extends Material | Material[] = Material> extends Object3D { … }
```

- `constructor(geometry?: BufferGeometry, material?: TMaterial);`
- `geometry: BufferGeometry;`

- `material: TMaterial;`

  Since API\_MINOR 17 also an array of materials (three.js's multi-material meshes): each of the geometry's groups drawn with the material at its `materialIndex` (a group whose material is missing or not `visible` draws nothing, and without groups nothing draws). Each group draws as an object of its own, an indexed geometry's groups each uploading the geometry's vertices (keep the attributes' arrays: one released after upload cannot make the groups again). Rays hit the groups' triangles. An InstancedMesh takes one material. (`Mesh<Material[]>`, as `new Mesh(geometry, [a, b])` infers, types it as an array; three.js's own typings say `Material | Material[]`.)

- `getVertexPosition(index: number, target: Vector3): Vector3;`

  Vertex `index`'s model-space position (since API\_MINOR 18), morphed by the influences since host API 1.40.

- `morphTargetInfluences?: number[];`

  Morph targets (since host API 1.40, three.js r185's): each target's influence (0 to start), made by `updateMorphTargets` (the constructor calls it) when the geometry has `morphAttributes`; undefined otherwise. Animate them with `.morphTargetInfluences[name]` tracks or glTF `weights` channels.

- `morphTargetDictionary?: Record<string, number>;`

  Each target's index by its attribute's `name` (or its index as a string; glTF's `extras.targetNames`).

- `updateMorphTargets(): void;`

  Makes `morphTargetInfluences` and `morphTargetDictionary` for the geometry's morph attributes (call it after giving a mesh a geometry with targets). Since host API 1.40.

### Skeleton

*class*

Bones and the inverses of their bind-pose world matrices (since API\_MINOR 25). The runtime computes each frame's bone matrices from the scene's world transforms (`bone.matrixWorld × boneInverses[i]`), so there is no bone count limit short of 4,096; `update` fills `boneMatrices` the same way for the script. Changing an inverse in place takes effect at the next `calculateInverses`, `init` or bind.

```ts
export class Skeleton { … }
```

- `constructor(bones?: Bone[], boneInverses?: Matrix4[]);`
- `uuid: string;`
- `bones: Bone[];`
- `boneInverses: Matrix4[];`
- `boneMatrices: Float32Array;`

- `boneTexture: null;`

  Always null: the bone matrices live in the runtime's texture.

- `init(): void;`
- `calculateInverses(): void;`
- `pose(): void;`
- `update(): void;`
- `clone(): Skeleton;`

- `computeBoneTexture(): this;`

- `getBoneByName(name: string): Bone | undefined;`

### SkinnedMesh

*class*

A mesh whose vertices its skeleton's bones move (since API\_MINOR 25): the geometry's `skinIndex` and `skinWeight` attributes (four joints and weights a vertex) skin it in every material's vertex stage, custom materials' hooks (before the game's vertex hook) and shadows and the depth and normal prepasses included, as three.js's `skinning_vertex` does. It culls by `boundingSphere`, made from its posed vertices the first time it is drawn with `frustumCulled` (three.js), and rays hit its geometry as bound.

```ts
export class SkinnedMesh<TMaterial extends Material | Material[] = Material> extends Mesh<TMaterial> { … }
```

  "attached" (the default: `bindMatrixInverse` follows the mesh's world matrix) or "detached".

- `bindMatrixInverse: Matrix4;`

- `boundingSphere: Sphere | null;`

## Host API 1.40's animation extensions (the engine's; three.js has none of these)

### CompressClipOptions

*interface*

```ts
export interface CompressClipOptions { … }
```

- `fps?: number;`

  Keys a second the tracks are resampled at (30).

- `rotationTolerance?: number;`

  A quaternion track whose keys all lie this close to its first keeps one key (1e-4).

- `translationTolerance?: number;`

  A vector or number track whose keys all lie this close to its first keeps one key (1e-4).

### compressClip

*function*

```ts
export function compressClip(clip: AnimationClip, options?: CompressClipOptions): AnimationClip;
```

The engine's extension (since host API 1.40), after the Animation Compression Library: the clip resampled at `fps`, quaternion tracks kept in 48 bits a key (their three smallest components), vector and number tracks in 16 bits a component over each track's own range, a track that does not move as one key. A third of the memory or less; the mixer and AnimationGraph play it as any clip (errors about 1e-4 of a quaternion component and 1/131,070 of a track's range). String, boolean and color tracks are kept as they are.

```ts

```

### AnimationGraphDefinition

*interface*

```ts
export interface AnimationGraphDefinition { … }
```

- `clips: Record<string, AnimationClip | { clip: AnimationClip; loop?: boolean }>;`

  Clips by the graph's names; a looping one (the default) wraps, `loop: false` holds its end.

- `parameters?: Record<string, number>;`

- `notifies?: { clip: string; time: number; name: string }[];`

  `notify` events as a layer's dominant clip crosses `time` (seconds into it), each wrap of a long step too.

- `layers: AnimationGraphLayerDefinition[];`

- `fixedStep?: number;`

  Seconds a step (0: one step an update). With it, transitions and notifies fall alike at any frame rate (and alike natively and in browsers), the pose between steps looked ahead to.

### AnimationGraph

*class*

The engine's extension (since host API 1.40), after Solstice's animation graphs: a state machine of clips over an object's tree, each layer's states playing a clip or blending clips by parameters, its transitions fading when a parameter's test holds (a change mid-fade fading on from the pose as it stood), sync groups, notifies from the dominant clip, and layers over the base masked by bone branches, overriding or additive. It samples and blends the clips itself and sets the bound properties (Object3D positions, quaternions, scales, `morphTargetInfluences`, material numbers) as the mixer would; it uses no AnimationMixer. Events: `notify` (\{ name, clip, state, layer \}).

```ts
export class AnimationGraph extends EventDispatcher { … }
```

- `constructor(root: Object3D, definition: AnimationGraphDefinition);`
- `readonly root: Object3D;`

- `fixedStep: number;`

  Seconds a step (see `AnimationGraphDefinition.fixedStep`).

- `static parse(text: string, clips: AnimationClip[] | Record<string, AnimationClip>): AnimationGraphDefinition;`

  Solstice's `.anim` text as a definition, its clips by source name from `clips`: `clip NAME SOURCE [loop|once]`, `notify CLIP TIME NAME`, `param NAME VALUE`, `state NAME clip CLIP`, `state NAME blend1d PARAM AT CLIP ...`, `state NAME blend2d X Y AT_X AT_Y CLIP ...`, `start STATE`, `transition FROM|* TO PARAM OP VALUE fade SECONDS`; the engine's `layer NAME [override|additive] [weight W] [mask BONE ...]` (the lines after it are that layer's), `sync STATE GROUP`, `speed STATE N` and `step SECONDS`. `source` and `roles` lines are skipped; `#` starts a comment. A mistake throws a SyntaxError naming its line.

- `getParameter(name: string): number;`

- `setParameter(name: string, value: number): boolean;`

  False for a parameter the graph lacks or a value that is not finite.

- `readonly state: string;`

  The base layer's state.

- `stateOf(layer?: number | string): string;`

- `phaseOf(layer?: number | string): number;`

  How far through its cycle a layer's state is, 0 to 1.

- `setLayerWeight(layer: number | string, weight: number): this;`

- `goTo(state: string, fade?: number, layer?: number | string): boolean;`

  Fades a layer to a state now, whatever its transitions say (false for a state it lacks).

- `update(delta: number): string[];`

  Moves the clock on by `delta` seconds (in fixed steps when `fixedStep` is set) and sets the pose; gives the notifies fired, in order.

- `evaluate(): this;`

  Sets the pose as it stands now.

- `setUpdateIntervals(levels: AnimationUpdateInterval[] | null, camera?: Object3D): this;`

  The pose set at most every `interval` seconds of the root's distance level from the camera (the renderer's, or `camera`); the clock and notifies keep every step. Null: every update.

- `stop(): this;`

  The bound properties back at the values they had when the graph was made.

### RetargetOptions

*interface*

```ts
export interface RetargetOptions { … }
```

- `preserveBoneMatrix?: boolean;`

- `preserveHipPosition?: boolean;`

  Leave the hip where it is.

- `useTargetMatrix?: boolean;`

- `hip?: string;`

  The hip's (pelvis's) name without role files ("hip").

- `hipInfluence?: Vector3;`

- `scale?: number;`

  How far the hip travels for the source's (the leg-length ratio with role files, else 1).

- `names?: Record<string, string>;`

  Target bone name to source bone name.

- `getBoneName?: (bone: Bone) => string;`
- `hipPosition?: Vector3;`

- `roles?: { source: string | Record<string, string[]>; target: string | Record<string, string[]> };`

  The engine's: both rigs' role files (text or `parseRoles`'s maps). With them bones pair by role and place along their chains, arm and leg chains are lined up at rest first (the hand by its palm, the fingers with it), rotations are carried across in each bone's rest frame, and the pelvis travels by the ratio of leg lengths. Without, bones pair by name.

- `useFirstFramePosition?: boolean;`

  retargetClip's: the hip's first position taken off every frame's.

- `fps?: number;`

  retargetClip's keys a second (30).

- `trim?: [number, number];`

  retargetClip's start and end seconds.

### SkeletonUtils

*const*

```ts
export const SkeletonUtils: {
    /** Poses `target`'s skeleton as `source`'s stands now. */
    retarget(target: SkinnedMesh | Object3D, source: SkinnedMesh | Object3D | Skeleton, options?: RetargetOptions): void;
    /** `clip` played on `source` carried onto `target`'s skeleton as a new clip sampled at `fps`: each paired
     * bone's `.bones[NAME].quaternion` and the hip's `.position`. */
    retargetClip(target: SkinnedMesh | Object3D, source: SkinnedMesh | Object3D, clip: AnimationClip, options?: RetargetOptions): AnimationClip;
    /** A copy of the tree whose skinned meshes are bound to the copy's own bones. */
    clone<T extends Object3D>(source: T): T;
  };
```

Null: every update again.

### InstancedMesh

*class*

One geometry and material drawn `count` times with per-instance transforms and colors. A game's instanced meshes hold at most 262,144 instances together (their capacities), and a frame draws what their `count`s say; since API\_MINOR 9 they no longer count toward the 65,536 meshes and points a game holds (before, each instance of the capacity did, and the bound was 65,536 for everything).

```ts
export class InstancedMesh extends Mesh<Material> { … }
```

- `constructor(geometry: BufferGeometry, material: Material, count: number);`

- `count: number;`

  Instances drawn, at most the constructor's count.

- `readonly instanceMatrix: BufferAttribute;`

  16 floats an instance (column-major matrices), as three.js: write the array and set `needsUpdate` (optionally with an update range) to send the changed instances in one host call.

- `readonly instanceColor: BufferAttribute | null;`

  3 floats an instance (linear RGB, default white), as `instanceMatrix`; null until `setColorAt` is first called.

- `instanceCustom: BufferAttribute | null;`

  4, 8, 12 or 16 floats an instance (up to four vec4s, default zeros) that custom materials read as `Vertex.instance` and `instance1` to `instance3`, as `instanceMatrix`; null until `setCustomAt` is first called (since API\_MINOR 7).

  THE STRIDE: instance i's slot k starts at `i * itemSize + k * 4`. `setCustomAt` makes it `customSlots` vec4s an instance, and without `customSlots` FOUR: 16 floats an instance even when only slot 0 is used (it says so once in the console). Code that writes the array itself must use `itemSize`, or declare `customSlots` first (1 for 4 floats an instance). Since API\_MINOR 9 an array of another stride than the declared slots', or whose length is not the capacity times its stride, is a TypeError at `setCustomAt` and at the frame's sync, where it used to draw garbage. Culled, the engine draws instances in an order of its own: to tell them apart, keep an index here (or set `frustumCulled` false).

- `customSlots: number | undefined;`

  Since API\_MINOR 9: the custom vec4 slots each instance keeps (1 to 4; a RangeError at `setCustomAt` otherwise), so `instanceCustom` is `customSlots × 4` floats an instance: 1 keeps 4 where `setCustomAt` would make 16. Set it before the first `setCustomAt`; a slot past it is a RangeError, slots past it read as zeros, and an `instanceCustom` of another stride is a TypeError. Undefined (the default) keeps API\_MINOR 7's four slots.

- `setMatrixAt(index: number, matrix: Matrix4): void;`
- `getMatrixAt(index: number, target: Matrix4): void;`

- `setColorAt(index: number, color: Color): void;`

  Multiplies the material color (default white).

- `getColorAt(index: number, target: Color): void;`

- `setCustomAt(index: number, value: Vector4, slot?: number): void;`

  Custom vec4 `slot` (0 to 3, default 0) of an instance (since API\_MINOR 7).

- `getCustomAt(index: number, target: Vector4, slot?: number): void;`

- `boundingBox: Box3 | null;`

  The box and sphere around its first `count` instances (three.js; since API\_MINOR 18; null until computed).

- `boundingSphere: Sphere | null;`
- `computeBoundingBox(): void;`
- `computeBoundingSphere(): void;`

- `readonly levels: readonly InstanceLevel[];`

  ENGINE EXTENSION, not three.js (since API\_MINOR 26; three.js's InstancedMesh and BatchedMesh have no levels of detail): its farther levels, nearest first. Level 0 is its own geometry and material.

- `setLevels(levels: readonly InstanceLevel[]): this;`

  ENGINE EXTENSION, not three.js (since API\_MINOR 26): per-instance levels of detail. Every frame the runtime gives each instance the level of its world distance from the camera it draws (the last level whose `distance` it reaches; the camera's `zoom` is not applied) and draws each level as an instanced batch of its own, its instances bucketed natively; shadow maps draw the level the camera sees. The buckets are made again only when an instance changes level or the instances change, so a still camera costs a distance per instance. A level with `geometry: null` draws nothing (a draw distance beyond which instances are culled), `material` defaults to the mesh's own, and `hysteresis` keeps an instance at a level until that fraction of its distance nearer (three.js `LOD`'s rule). At most 7 levels at finite, non-decreasing distances (else a RangeError); `[]` removes them. Levels draw their whole geometry (the draw range is level 0's); culled, an instance's order within a level is the engine's. Clones and copies share the levels.

```

- `readonly material?: Material;`
- `readonly distance: number;`
- `readonly hysteresis?: number;`

## Levels of detail generation (since API\_MINOR 40)

### SimplifyModifier

*class*

three.js r185's addon `SimplifyModifier` (examples/jsm/modifiers/SimplifyModifier.js), exported here as the engine has no addons path (since API\_MINOR 40; before it the constructor is a TypeError). `modify(geometry, count)` gives a new indexed geometry with `count` fewer vertices, counted as three.js counts them after merging vertices whose position, uv, normal, tangent and color agree within 1e-4 (`BufferGeometryUtils.mergeVertices`), and those attributes as Float32 attributes; morph targets, groups and other attributes go, as in three.js. A count of 0 (or NaN) removes none; a count that never counts down to 0 (negative, fractional, Infinity) as many as can go. DIFFERENCE: the engine chooses what goes by quadric error (half-edge collapse after Solstice's builder: every surviving vertex is an original one, UV seams and hard edges keep their sides' attributes, open borders never move, and a texture sliding counts as error) rather than three.js's Melax cost, so the triangles differ from three.js's for the same count. The same input gives the same output bits natively and in browsers.

```ts
export class SimplifyModifier { … }
```

- `constructor();`
- `modify(geometry: BufferGeometry, count: number): BufferGeometry;`

### GenerateLodsOptions

*interface*

ENGINE EXTENSION: `generateLods`'s options.

```ts
export interface GenerateLodsOptions { … }
```

- `levels?: number;`

  Levels made beyond the mesh's own: 1 to 16 (default 3; an InstancedMesh takes at most 7). Fewer come back where another level would not drop a twentieth of the triangles.

- `ratio?: number;`

  Each level's triangles as a fraction of the one before, above 0 and below 1 (default 0.5).

- `errorPx?: number;`

  The most pixels a level may be off where it shows (default 1).

- `thin?: boolean;`

  Thin a mesh of many (8 or more) separate small pieces, such as grass blades or leaves: each level keeps about `ratio` of the pieces (spread evenly by where they are, each level's among the last's) and enlarges the survivors, flat ones across first, tubes thicker, so the total area stays the same (default false). Pieces much wider than most, and the rest of the mesh, simplify as usual.

- `camera?: PerspectiveCamera;`

  The camera whose `fov` the distances are for (default a fov of 50, PerspectiveCamera's default).

- `screenHeight?: number;`

  The viewport height in pixels the distances are for (default 1080).

- `hysteresis?: number;`

  Each level's hysteresis, as `LOD.addLevel` takes it (default 0).

### generateLods

*function*

```ts
export function generateLods(mesh: InstancedMesh, options?: GenerateLodsOptions): InstancedMesh;
```

ENGINE EXTENSION (since API\_MINOR 40; before it a TypeError): levels of detail from a mesh's simplified geometries, made by quadric half-edge collapse as `SimplifyModifier` makes them, every surviving vertex keeping all its own attributes (UV seams, normals, colors, tangents and skin weights exactly) and open borders kept. Each level has about `ratio` of the triangles of the one before and its error in world units (the farthest any source vertex lies from it, how far a texture slid or changed weights could move a vertex, how far thinning moved one; more than the level before's, a level no farther off replacing it so no two switch at one distance) in its geometry's `userData.lodError`. A level shows from the camera distance where that error spans `errorPx` pixels on a `screenHeight`-pixel viewport: `error × screenHeight / (2 tan(fov / 2) × errorPx)`.

For a Mesh: a three.js `LOD` taking the mesh's name and transform, level 0 a mesh of its own geometry and each further level one of a simplified geometry, all sharing its material and shadow flags (a SkinnedMesh's levels are SkinnedMeshes bound to its skeleton); the mesh itself is left as it was. For a BufferGeometry: the same with a new MeshStandardMaterial. For an InstancedMesh: `setLevels` with the simplified geometries and their distances, and the mesh back. A geometry with more than one group is a TypeError (one group, as built-in shapes have, carries over as a group of the whole level). The work is native, charged to the call's fuel in proportion to what it did; a geometry has at most 1,048,576 vertices and triangles (RangeError).

```ts
export function generateLods(target: Mesh | BufferGeometry, options?: GenerateLodsOptions): LOD;
```

### ParticleVector

*type*

export type ParticleVector = { x: number; y: number; z: number } | readonly [number, number, number];
```

### ParticleEmitterOptions

*interface*

A `ParticleEmitter`'s settings (since API\_MINOR 37). Vectors are in the emitter's space: its axes and scale.

```ts
export interface ParticleEmitterOptions { … }
```

- `capacity?: number;`

  The most particles alive at once, 1 to 16,384 (default 256). Fixed when made; a game's emitters hold at most 32,768 together and a game has at most 256 emitters (a RangeError past either).

- `material?: Material;`

  Point sprites: a `PointsMaterial` (default: a new one). Instanced: any mesh material (default: a new `MeshBasicMaterial`).

- `geometry?: BufferGeometry | null;`

  Draws each particle as an instance of this geometry (default null: point sprites).

- `seed?: number;`

  The random stream's seed, an integer 0 to 2^32 − 1 (default 1).

- `rate?: number;`

  Particles a second, spread evenly through each frame (default 0: only bursts).

- `life?: number | readonly [number, number];`

  A particle's life in seconds, or \[min, max\] (uniformly between; 0.001 to 3600; default 1). Since API\_MINOR 40 longer lives too, and `Infinity` (alone or as the longer end): every particle lives until cleared, its ramps held at their first values.

- `space?: "world" | "local";`

  "world" (default): particles spawn where the emitter is and stay in the world as it moves on. "local": they move with it.

- `shape?: "point" | "box" | "sphere" | "shell" | "ring" | "disc";`

  Where particles start round the emitter's origin (or a burst's point): "point" (default), "box" (anywhere within ±`extent` on each axis), "sphere" (anywhere within radius `extent`) or "shell" (on that sphere). Since API\_MINOR 40 also "ring" (on a circle of radius `extent` in the emitter's XZ plane) and "disc" (anywhere within it).

- `extent?: number | ParticleVector;`

  The box's half extents (a number: a cube) or the sphere's radius.

- `velocity?: ParticleVector;`

  A spawned particle's velocity (units a second; default 0), plus up to ±`velocitySpread` on each axis, plus a speed from `speed` along a direction within `spread` radians of `direction` (π: any).

- `velocitySpread?: number | ParticleVector;`

- `speed?: number | readonly [number, number];`

  A number, or \[min, max\] (default 0).

- `direction?: ParticleVector;`

  Default \[0, 1, 0\].

- `spread?: number;`

  0 to π radians (default 0).

- `gravity?: ParticleVector;`

  Acceleration in units a second squared (default 0).

- `drag?: number;`

  Each frame's velocity is divided by 1 + drag × delta (default 0).

- `size?: number | readonly number[];`

  A size factor, or 1 to 8 of them evenly spaced over each life (default 1). Points: times the material's `size` (pixels, or with `sizeAttenuation` world units as three.js's PointsMaterial). Instances: the instance's scale.

- `color?: ColorInput;`

  The particles' color (default white; linear values above 1 bloom): multiplies the material's color.

- `colors?: readonly ColorInput[];`

  1 to 8 colors evenly spaced over each life, in place of `color`.

- `opacity?: number | readonly number[];`

  0 to 1, or 1 to 8 values evenly spaced over each life (default 1): multiplies the material's opacity (a `transparent` material shows it).

- `twinkle?: ParticleTwinkle | null;`

  Since API\_MINOR 38 (an unknown option before): each particle's own oscillation, a star's twinkle (default null: none).

- `scale?: number | ParticleVector;`

  Since API\_MINOR 38: instances' scale on each axis, times `size` (default 1; 0 to 4,096). Point sprites leave it out.

- `scaleSpread?: number | ParticleVector;`

  Since API\_MINOR 38: up to ± this much of `scale` on each axis, a factor of each particle's own (default 0; never below 0), so pieces of debris differ in shape.

Since API\_MINOR 40 (PARTICLE\_FORCES\_MINOR; unknown options before). Forces and colliders act in the particles' space: the world's, or the emitter's with `space: "local"`. Wind, curl and the vortex move the air, which carries a particle through its `drag` (without drag they do nothing), as Solstice's particles do. An emitter using any of these steps its particles one at a time (no column layout), still deterministically, natively and in browsers alike.

- `wind?: ParticleVector;`

  The air's velocity (units a second; default 0).

- `curl?: number | ParticleCurl | null;`

  Curl noise moving the air (swirls that neither bunch particles up nor thin them out): a strength (units a second), or \{ strength, scale (feature size, default 4), change (cells a second, default 0.2) \}; null none.

- `buoyancy?: number;`

  Upward acceleration at birth, fading to none at the end of its life (hot gas; default 0).

- `vortex?: number;`

  The air turning about `direction` through the emitter's origin, radians a second (default 0).

- `attract?: number;`

  Acceleration towards the emitter's origin (default 0).

- `floor?: number | (ParticleCollider & { height?: number }) | null;`

  A floor: its height (a +Y plane particles slide along, "clamp"), or a collider with a `height` (default null: none).

- `colliders?: readonly ParticleCollider[] | null;`

  Planes and heightfields, at most 4 with the floor.

- `sway?: number | ParticleSway | null;`

  A wobble drawn about each particle's path (it does not move the particle): an amplitude, or \{ amplitude (a number or per axis; x and y follow a sine, z its cosine, so equal x and z sway in a circle), frequency (cycles a second, or \[min, max\], each particle its own; default 1) \}. Each particle has its own phase, hashed as twinkle's.

- `velocityMode?: "cone" | "planar" | "radial";`

  How `speed` is pointed: "cone" (default: within `spread` of `direction`), "planar" (anywhere in the plane across `direction`: a ring of spray) or "radial" (out from the origin through the spawn point, `direction` at the origin).

- `sizeSpread?: number;`

  Each particle's size times 1 ± this (0 to 1, its own factor).

- `lit?: boolean;`

  Point sprites lit as surfaces are (default false): camera-facing quads `material.size` world units across with a Lambert material made from the PointsMaterial (its color, map, opacity, blending), lit by the sun through its shadow maps with a Henyey–Greenstein phase (`phase`), by the environment and ambient light, and by the scene's other lights as a quad facing the camera. Every light a lit material takes reaches them (up to 16 a frame, each through its own shadow maps where the emitter receives shadows); unlike Solstice's particles, which trace only the two strongest lights at each particle past walls, no light is picked out or traced. GPU emitters' lit particles are lit the same way. ENGINE EXTENSION.

- `soft?: number;`

  Point sprites fading into the scene where they meet it, over this many units of view depth (`renderer.sceneDepth`; default 0: none): camera-facing quads as with `lit`, blended. ENGINE EXTENSION.

- `phase?: number;`

  A lit particle's scattering asymmetry, −1 to 1 (default 0.2: mostly onward, so mist glows with the sun behind it).

- `billboard?: boolean;`

  Point sprites as camera-facing quads `material.size` world units across, unlit (default false; `lit` and `soft` draw so too), as GPU emitters draw theirs. ENGINE EXTENSION.

- `rotation?: number;`

  Since API\_MINOR 40 (`PARTICLE_ROTATION_MINOR`; an unknown option before): each particle's angle as it spawns, in radians (default 0; −10^6 to 10^6), plus up to ± `rotationSpread` of its own (default 0; π: any angle). With `spin` it turns at `spin` radians a second (the same range; default 0), plus up to ± `spinSpread` of its own (default 0), so confetti flutters each at its own pace: its angle at age a is its start plus its spin × a (no drag, no ramp). Each particle's share of the spreads (and its axis) is hashed from its spawn number and the seed, never drawn from the random stream, so nothing else about the particles changes and live ones turn too. Point sprites (and `lit`, `soft` or `billboard` quads) turn in the view about their centres, counterclockwise on the screen for a positive angle (as three.js's `SpriteMaterial.rotation`), their `map` with them; instances turn about `rotationAxis`.

- `rotationSpread?: number;`
- `spin?: number;`
- `spinSpread?: number;`

- `rotationAxis?: ParticleVector | null;`

  Since API\_MINOR 40: the axis instances turn about, in the particles' space (made a unit vector; not zero). Default null: each particle an axis of its own, uniform over the sphere, so debris tumbles. Point sprites and their quads ignore it.

*interface*

A per-particle oscillation (since API\_MINOR 38). Each particle has a phase and a frequency of its own, hashed from its spawn number and the seed (the random stream is untouched, and live particles twinkle as soon as it is set). Its opacity is multiplied by `1 − opacity × w` and its size by `1 − size × w`, w going 0 → 1 → 0 once a cycle.

  0 to 1 (default 0).

## Audio in the scene (three.js r185's audio objects, host API 1.37)

starhermit:audio's graph placed by the scene: an `AudioListener` (on a camera, usually) moves `context.listener`, and each `PositionalAudio` its PannerNode, once a frame after the scene's sync, ramping to where their objects are over the frame's delta as three.js does (a PositionalAudio only while it plays). They need starhermit:audio imported and `SPATIAL_AUDIO_MINOR` (37): a TypeError otherwise. Buffers are starhermit:audio's `AudioBuffer`s (`context.decodeAudioData`, `createBuffer`); sounds of clips placed in 3D are `play(clip, { position })`, which follow the same listener.

### ParticleEmitter

*class*

Since API\_MINOR 37 (`PARTICLE_EMITTER_MINOR`; constructing one in an older game throws a TypeError): a pool of particles the runtime itself spawns, moves (velocity, gravity, drag), colors, fades and sizes over their lives and draws, once a frame after `onRender` and the scene's sync, so a game pays nothing in script per particle. Add it to the scene as any object; set it up once and change it now and then (`set`, `rate`), and `burst` it. Without a `geometry` its particles are point sprites drawn with its `PointsMaterial`; with one they are instances of it. Seeded and stepped by the frame's delta (the delta `onUpdate` gets, at most 0.25 s a frame), with the engine's own arithmetic, so the same frames give the same particles natively and in browsers: replays and render checks repeat. A step costs the frame's fuel one unit an emitter and one each 8 live particles. Points of all emitters together count toward a frame's 65,536 points, instances toward the instanced meshes' budget.

```ts
export class ParticleEmitter extends Object3D { … }
```

- `constructor(options?: ParticleEmitterOptions);`
- `readonly isParticleEmitter: true;`
- `material: Material;`
- `geometry: BufferGeometry | null;`

- `readonly capacity: number;`

  Fixed when made.

- `seed: number;`

  Changing it starts the random stream again.

- `rate: number;`

  Particles a second.

- `paused: boolean;`

  A paused emitter neither moves nor spawns (its particles still draw).

- `readonly count: number;`

  Its live particles, as of the last frame's step.

- `readonly options: ParticleEmitterOptions;`

  A copy of its settings.

- `set(options: ParticleEmitterOptions): this;`

  Changes some settings (all but `capacity`); the live particles stay and keep their lives. Since API\_MINOR 40 a set the range check refuses (a RangeError) leaves every setting as it was (before, the refused values stayed and the next frame's sync threw).

- `burst(count?: number, at?: ParticleVector, options?: ParticleBurstOptions): this;`

  Spawns `count` particles (default 1) at the next step, at `at` in the emitter's space (default its origin) plus the shape's offset. Past the capacity they are dropped. At most 256 bursts wait for a step: since API\_MINOR 40 one more is a RangeError (before, it was dropped).

- `prewarm(seconds: number): this;`

  Since API\_MINOR 38 (absent before): runs it `seconds` (0 to 600) ahead now, from where it is, as frames of at most 0.25 s would, paused or not, so a steady emitter starts full. Charged as those steps (one unit each and one each 8 particles), each before it runs. Since API\_MINOR 40 it runs the settings a `set` made this frame (1.38 and 1.39 ran the last frame's until the sync sent them).

- `clear(): this;`

  Lets every live particle go.

- `dispose(): void;`

  Lets its particles and its capacity go; it draws nothing after.

### TextLabelOptions

*interface*

A `TextLabel`'s settings (since API\_MINOR 37). Sizes in font sizes are fractions of `size`.

```ts
export interface TextLabelOptions { … }
```

- `text?: string;`

- `size?: number;`

  The font size: world units (default 0.5), or CSS pixels with `units: "pixels"` (default 16).

- `units?: "world" | "pixels";`

  `"world"` (default): it is sized in the scene and shrinks with distance; `"pixels"`: the same size on screen at any distance (a billboard only).

- `billboard?: boolean;`

  Faces the camera (default, as a Sprite), or false: lies in the object's xy plane facing +z and turns with it.

- `depthTest?: boolean;`

  Hidden behind nearer surfaces (default); false draws it over them (raise `renderOrder` to draw it over other transparent objects).

- `color?: ColorLike;`

  Default white.

- `font?: string;`

  A CSS font family list (default "sans-serif"): the engine's fonts and those the game added (`starhermit:canvas` fonts), as a canvas `font` names them (`"'StarHermit Emoji', sans-serif"` draws the engine's emoji font's symbols first).

- `weight?: string | number;`

  A CSS font weight (default "normal").

- `style?: string;`

  "normal" (default) or "italic".

- `outlineColor?: ColorLike;`

  Default black.

- `outlineWidth?: number;`

  The outline round the glyphs, in font sizes (default 0: none).

- `background?: ColorLike | null;`

  A rounded box behind the text (default none).

- `padding?: number;`

  Space round the text, in font sizes (default 0.2).

- `radius?: number;`

  The background's corner radius, in font sizes (default 0.25).

- `align?: "left" | "center" | "right";`

  Lines (split at "\\n") aligned within the widest (default "center").

- `lineHeight?: number;`

  Line spacing, in font sizes (default 1.2).

- `anchor?: readonly [number, number] | { x: number; y: number };`

  The label's point at its position: \[0, 0\] its bottom left, \[1, 1\] its top right (default \[0.5, 0.5\]; `center` for a billboard, as Sprite's).

- `resolution?: number;`

  World labels: texture pixels a font size (default 64). Pixel labels are laid out at the window's scale, a texture pixel a window pixel. A label larger than a canvas may be (4096 pixels a side, 2^23 in all) is laid out scaled down to fit, as large but coarser.

- `opacity?: number;`

  The material's opacity (default 1).

### TextLabel

*class*

Text in the scene (since API\_MINOR 37, `TEXT_LABELS_MINOR`; older games' constructor throws a TypeError), for names, scores and tile numerals without a canvas bake in script: the runtime lays the text out with the engine's text stack (shaping, fallback fonts, emoji, as canvas text) into a texture of the label's own in one call, and again only when what it shows changes (its text, font, colors, outline, background, padding, alignment or resolution; not its position, world size, depth test or opacity). Add it to the scene like any object; it draws as a Sprite (`billboard`, the default) or as a plane mesh, with a SpriteMaterial or MeshBasicMaterial whose `map` is its texture (not tone mapped, no fog, transparent, not writing depth).

Like three-spritetext's `SpriteText`, the label sets its own `scale` from its text: size it with `size`. A world label's line is `size` world units of font; a pixel label (`units: "pixels"`) is `size` CSS pixels of font whatever its distance, fitted after `onRender` to the window's camera (`renderer.camera`) and the window's height (in other cameras' views it keeps that scale). It has no raycast. Each label holds a canvas and a texture image (against the game's canvas and image budgets) until `dispose()`, or until it is collected (a label that finds no room in the canvas budget releases dropped ones first). Settings that throw (`set`, the setters) leave it as it was.

```ts
export class TextLabel extends Object3D { … }
```

- `constructor(text?: string, options?: TextLabelOptions);`
- `constructor(options: TextLabelOptions);`
- `readonly isTextLabel: true;`

- `text: string;`

  The text shown; setting the same text again lays nothing out.

- `readonly material: SpriteMaterial | MeshBasicMaterial;`

  What draws it (its own; replaced as `billboard` changes).

- `readonly geometry: BufferGeometry;`

  A fixed label's plane (shared by labels of its anchor).

- `readonly center: Vector2;`

  Its anchor, as Sprite's `center`.

- `readonly options: TextLabelOptions;`

  A copy of its settings.

- `set(options: TextLabelOptions): this;`

  Changes some settings; it lays out again only if what it shows changed.

- `readonly width: number;`

  Its size: world units for a world label, CSS pixels for a pixel label.

- `readonly height: number;`

- `dispose(): void;`

  Lets its texture, canvas and materials go; it draws nothing after.

  | "easeInQuart" | "easeOutQuart" | "easeInOutQuart"
  | "easeInQuint" | "easeOutQuint" | "easeInOutQuint"
  | "easeInSine" | "easeOutSine" | "easeInOutSine"
  | "easeInExpo" | "easeOutExpo" | "easeInOutExpo"
  | "easeInCirc" | "easeOutCirc" | "easeInOutCirc"
  | "easeInBack" | "easeOutBack" | "easeInOutBack"
  | "easeInElastic" | "easeOutElastic" | "easeInOutElastic"
